questions.q: What are the three lifecycle stages a code list value goes through, according to this lesson?
options: Imported, exported, compressed
Created, renamed, duplicated
Encrypted, hashed, archived
Added, deprecated, retired
questions.explain: Codes are added when a new valid value is needed, deprecated when no longer usable for new records (but still referenced historically), and retired when fully removed from active use.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say deleting a code outright is almost always the wrong move?
options: Because deletion only affects codes that were never actually used
Because every historical record that referenced the deleted code points at nothing, breaking reports or silently dropping rows
Because deleted codes automatically get re-added the next day
Because deleting a code is technically impossible in most databases
questions.explain: Historical records that referenced a deleted code lose a valid reference entirely, which is why deprecating (marking inactive but keeping the row) is almost always preferable.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an effective-from and effective-to date on a code table row, per this lesson?
options: To set an expiration date after which the entire database is deleted
To indicate how many times the code has been used in transactions
To specify which employee is allowed to view the code
To record the window during which that code's meaning or active status was the current, valid one
questions.explain: Effective dating lets a query determine what a code meant on the date a historical record was created, rather than applying today's understanding to old data.

questions.q: In the lesson's illustrative order-status example, what happened to the 'PEND' code when 'RVW' was introduced?
options: PEND was marked inactive with an effective_to date, but kept in the table so pre-2023 orders still resolve correctly
PEND was renamed to RVW across all historical records
PEND and RVW were merged into a single row
PEND was immediately deleted from the database
questions.explain: PEND's is_active flag became false and its effective_to date was set to 2023-06-30, but the row remained so orders placed before that date still have a valid status reference.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what discipline should govern changes to a code list in production?
options: Only the original developer who created the table may ever modify it
Code list changes require no approval since the data set is small
A defined owner, a documented reason for each change, and a predictable release process
Any employee should be able to edit the code table directly whenever convenient
questions.explain: The lesson argues a typo in a reference table is just as damaging as a bug in application code, so code list changes need the same rigor as any other governed change.
